hook: A car at highway speed and the same car in a parking lot differ in one number on the speedometer, but the faster one needs far more road to stop. Kinetic energy explains why: it grows with the square of the speed, so modest speed increases have outsized consequences.

prereq.q: Which of these is a scalar?
prereq.why: Speed has a size but no direction; the other three are vectors.

prereq.q: A cart moves west at 3.0 m/s, with east positive. What is its speed?
prereq.why: Speed is the size of the velocity, so it is positive: 3.0 m/s.

prereq.q: From v² = v₀² + 2aΔx, a car that stops (v = 0) with a constant deceleration of size a travels

figure.caption: The same car at 10 m/s and at 20 m/s. Twice the speed means four times the kinetic energy and, with the same brakes, four times the stopping distance.

chain.cause: An object of mass m moves at speed v
chain.effect: it has kinetic energy K = ½mv², measured in joules (kg·m²/s²)
doubling the speed makes K four times as large, while doubling the mass only doubles it

chain.cause: Squaring removes the sign of the velocity
chain.effect: K is a scalar that is never negative and does not depend on direction

chain.cause: Speed depends on the reference frame
chain.effect: the same object has different kinetic energies in different frames

chain.cause: A system has several moving parts
chain.effect: its kinetic energy is the sum of the parts' kinetic energies, which never cancel

ideas: Energy is a scalar quantity a system has; it can change form and move between objects. Its SI unit is the joule: 1 J = 1 kg·m²/s².
Kinetic energy, K = ½mv², is the energy of motion. It depends on mass and on the speed squared.
K is never negative and has no direction. A cart moving left at 3 m/s has the same K as one moving right at 3 m/s.
ΔK = ½mv_f² − ½mv_i², which is not ½m(Δv)². Square each speed first, then subtract.
Kinetic energy depends on the reference frame, because speed does.

misconception.wrong: A cart that speeds up from 1.5 m/s to 2.5 m/s gains ½m(1.0 m/s)² of kinetic energy.
misconception.right: The change is ½m(2.5 m/s)² − ½m(1.5 m/s)² = ½m(4.0 m²/s²), four times ½m(Δv)² = ½m(1.0 m²/s²). Square each speed before you subtract.

summary: Kinetic energy is K = ½mv², in joules. It is a scalar, never negative, independent of direction and dependent on the reference frame. Because the speed is squared, doubling the speed quadruples K; and a change in K is ½mv_f² − ½mv_i², not ½m(Δv)².
